title: Best Behavioral Health Billing Software (2026): 11 Options Compared
summary: The best behavioral health billing software in 2026: 11 options compared, from therapy practice suites to SUD treatment center RCM, with fit and watch-outs.
body_markdown:
The best behavioral health billing software depends on the kind of organization you run. Solo and group therapy or psychiatry practices are usually best served by practice suites with billing built in, such as TherapyNotes, SimplePractice, Valant and Tebra. SUD treatment centers need platforms that build claims from attendance or census data and track utilization review, such as Kipu Health and Sunwave Health (which now includes Lightning Step). Agencies and CCBHCs tend to evaluate Qualifacts and Netsmart, ABA providers look at CentralReach, and multi-specialty practices often consider AdvancedMD. Programs that want to keep their current EHR and billing system and automate the billing and coding work inside it can add Adentris.


All eleven handle the mechanics of getting a claim out the door. What separates them is fit: the claim types they are built around, how they handle levels of care and authorizations, and whether the vendor also offers billing staff. Descriptions come from each vendor's own website as of October 2026; the list is grouped by type, not ranked.


The short version


- Choose by organization type and levels of care first; a feature list matters less than whether the system is built for the way you bill.
- Outpatient therapy and psychiatry practices fit practice suites: TherapyNotes, SimplePractice, Valant, Tebra and AdvancedMD. Valant also supports 837i institutional claims for IOP and PHP.
- SUD and residential treatment centers fit Kipu Health and Sunwave Health, which build claims from attendance or census data and track utilization review.
- Agencies and CCBHCs look at Qualifacts and Netsmart, which pair software with RCM teams. CentralReach covers ABA.
- A clean claim is not the same as a defensible claim. Pre-bill documentation review is a separate layer that works on top of any of these systems.


## How we chose


We chose established vendors whose own websites describe billing features in detail and name behavioral health as a core market, then checked four things:


- **Billing depth:** eligibility, claim creation and scrubbing, clearinghouse submission, ERA posting and denial follow-up.
- **Behavioral health fit:** group and session-based services, authorizations and utilization review, multiple programs, and institutional claims where IOP or PHP calls for them.
- **Who it is built for:** the organization types the vendor names.
- **Services option:** whether the vendor or its partners can also do the billing work.


Lightning Step was on our original list, but its website now states that it is part of Sunwave, so the two share one entry and we added CentralReach for ABA.


## What behavioral health billing software has to handle


Almost any billing system can submit a behavioral health claim. The differences are in the surrounding workflows:


- **Group and session-based services.** As Sunwave's site puts it, a single group session can generate a dozen individual claims. Look for charge capture from the schedule or attendance record and bulk claim creation.
- **Authorizations and utilization review.** Higher levels of care usually run on authorizations and concurrent review, so the system that builds claims should flag expiring authorizations before the claim denies.
- **Professional and institutional claims.** Some IOP and PHP billing uses institutional (837I) claims; if you bill both types, confirm the system handles both. See our[IOP and PHP billing guide](https://blog.adentris.com/iop-php-billing-documentation-guide/) .
- **Multiple programs and Tax IDs.** Fee schedules and billing identifiers set by payer and site.
- **SUD confidentiality.** 42 CFR Part 2 restricts the use and disclosure of SUD patient records kept by Part 2 programs, so consent status should be visible to whoever sends claims and records. See our[Part 2 consent guide](https://blog.adentris.com/42-cfr-part-2-consent-documentation-guide/) .
- **Denial follow-up.** ERA posting that routes denials into worklists by reason code and payer.

## 1. TherapyNotes


**What it is:** A practice management system and EHR built for behavioral health, from psychologists and therapists to psychiatrists and social workers, which the company says fits anyone from a solo psychologist to a large practice.


**Best for:** Solo clinicians and outpatient group practices that want insurance billing inside the EHR.


**Strengths:**


- An included clearinghouse with claims and updates from over 2,000 payers, plus real-time eligibility for nearly 900 payers
- Proprietary claim scrubbing, telehealth and supervision modifiers, and per-clinician billing overrides by payer
- Free ERA enrollment with assisted posting, aging reports, prior authorization renewal reports, and optional billing services through partners


**Watch-outs:**


- Billing is described around professional claims (electronic claims and CMS-1500 forms), so programs billing IOP, PHP or residential care on institutional claims should ask how those are handled.
- Outsourced billing runs through partner firms, a second company to evaluate.


## 2. SimplePractice


**What it is:** An EHR and practice management platform for health and wellness professionals, including therapists, psychiatrists, speech-language pathologists and occupational therapists, in solo and group practices.


**Best for:** Solo and small group private practices, including clinicians new to accepting insurance.


**Strengths:**


- Create, submit, track, reconcile and invoice claims in one place, with integrated ERAs and automated ERA enrollment
- Batch in-network claims, claim rules that automate repetitive edits before submission, and a centralized billing hub
- Insurance Navigator adds phone access to Insurance Specialists, and the site advertises free credentialing with up to two payers for new sign-ups


**Watch-outs:**


- Built around private practice, so programs with residential, IOP or PHP levels of care should confirm fit.
- Insurance tools are packaged as Insurance Essentials and Insurance Navigator; check what each plan includes and how claims are priced.


## 3. Valant


**What it is:** A behavioral health EHR for outpatient care and higher-acuity outpatient programs such as IOP and PHP, used by solo clinicians, groups, multi-practice organizations and billing agencies.


**Best for:** Outpatient psychiatry and therapy groups, especially those running or adding IOP or PHP.


**Strengths:**


- Service bundling and direct submission of 837i institutional claims for IOP and PHP
- A Pending Transactions Queue and automated charge review that flag coding issues or missing information before claims are created
- Billing under different Tax IDs by payer or facility, plus optional RCM services covering claims, denials, appeals and payment posting


**Watch-outs:**


- Positioned for outpatient care up to IOP and PHP, so detox and residential programs should confirm their levels of care are supported.
- Valant describes its RCM team as working inside the Valant EHR, so the service assumes you are on Valant.


## 4. Adentris


*Disclosure: Adentris publishes this guide.*


**What it is:** An AI platform that runs the billing and coding workflow inside the systems you already use. It connects to your EHR and billing tools through their APIs, HL7 feeds, or the AI Web Agent, usually with no IT project on your side, so those systems stay your system of record. It codes every claim against the chart, checks each claim and chart against payer and regulatory rules before submission, builds prior authorization packets and tracks their windows, and works denials through root-cause clustering and rule-cited appeals.


**Best for:** Behavioral health and SUD programs, and other providers, that want to automate billing, coding and denial work without replacing their EHR or billing system.


**Strengths:**


- Works on top of any EHR and billing system and is typically live in about 30 days
- Every chart is checked before the claim goes out against BH and SUD rules such as ASAM level of care, medical necessity and 42 CFR Part 2, and each finding cites the rule that fired
- Coding, prior authorization, denials and appeals in one platform
- SOC 2 Type I and Type II, a signed BAA, and AI inference inside Microsoft Azure


**Watch-outs:**


- Not a standalone EHR or clearinghouse: it works through the EHR and billing tools you already have, so one of them remains your system of record.
- Deepest in behavioral health and SUD rules; other specialties should confirm their payers' rules are covered.


## 5. Kipu Health


**What it is:** A platform connecting CRM, EMR, RCM and compliance tools for substance use, behavioral health and eating disorder treatment centers and medication-assisted treatment programs.


**Best for:** SUD and behavioral health treatment centers with residential and multi-level programs.


**Strengths:**


- Kipu EMR pushes demographics and charges to Kipu RCM in one click, and claims are generated automatically from an Attendance Calendar of services rendered
- Utilization review alerts for new, incomplete, expired and soon-to-expire reviews, plus authorization alerts
- Real-time or batch eligibility checks, custom claim rules, automated ERA posting, and reports built for addiction treatment facilities


**Watch-outs:**


- Built around treatment center workflows, so an outpatient-only therapy practice may not need most of it.
- The billing integration is described around Kipu EMR; if you keep another EHR, ask how charges would flow.


## 6. Sunwave Health (including Lightning Step)


**What it is:** An AI-native EMR, CRM and RCM platform for behavioral health organizations, substance use treatment centers, mental health clinics and eating disorder centers. Sunwave says it and Lightning Step united in 2025, and Lightning Step's site says it is now part of Sunwave.


**Best for:** Treatment centers with high volumes of group, residential and multi-level billing that want one cloud-based system.


**Strengths:**


- Claims generated automatically from census and attendance data, with a rules engine and bulk actions
- Automatic error detection, real-time claim edits and status, and billing audits that match billables, invoices and remittances
- Utilization review management, VOB and claims dashboards, and self-pay, ACH and payment plan workflows


**Watch-outs:**


- Built for treatment organizations, so a solo therapist would use a small part of it.
- Lightning Step customers should ask how the combined company plans to support each platform.


## 7. Qualifacts


**What it is:** A behavioral health EHR company with three platforms (Credible, CareLogic and InSync) that says it is the EHR partner for 2,200+ behavioral health agencies. It lists CCBHCs, addiction treatment and IDD among the groups it serves.


**Best for:** Community behavioral health agencies, CCBHCs and multi-program SUD or IDD providers that want an optional co-sourced billing team.


**Strengths:**


- Claims created automatically after services, with automated coding and modifiers, claims scrubbing and batch processing
- Real-time and batch eligibility that detects coverage overlap and multiple payers
- A co-sourced RCM model in which its 200+ billing experts work in your EHR, with billing rules management, credentialing support and billing audits


**Watch-outs:**


- Features differ by platform (its iQ Agent for Billing is currently available on Credible), so confirm what applies to yours.
- Built primarily for agencies; small practices should compare its solo-practice offering with the suites above.


## 8. Netsmart


**What it is:** An EHR and services company for human services and post-acute care whose addiction treatment EHR supports MAT, OTP, OBOT and abstinence-based programs.


**Best for:** Large, multi-service organizations, including opioid treatment programs and CCBHCs, that want RCM services or collection automation at scale.


**Strengths:**


- RCM services from provider enrollment and eligibility through coding audits, billing, cash posting, denial and A/R management
- RevConnect for clearinghouse and eligibility, and AlphaCollector for collection automation with claim auto-statusing and denial guidance by CARC grouping
- Netsmart says its revenue cycle solutions are EHR-agnostic


**Watch-outs:**


- Some AI-assisted RCM functions are marked on its site as under development, so confirm what is available today.
- Built for large organizations; a small outpatient practice will likely find a better match among the practice suites.


## 9. CentralReach


**What it is:** An autism and IDD care platform for ABA and multidisciplinary therapy that combines EMR, practice management and AI-powered RCM.


**Best for:** ABA and autism or IDD therapy organizations, particularly multi-site and enterprise providers.


**Strengths:**


- Session note data converted to billing entries, with tracking of authorized hours to avoid over- or under-using authorizations
- ClaimCheckAI audits claims against payer-specific rules before submission, and ClaimAcceleratorAI classifies, prioritizes and routes denials
- CR BillMax, a managed billing service run by CentralReach billing experts inside the platform


**Watch-outs:**


- Built for autism, IDD and multidisciplinary therapy; mental health and SUD programs are outside its stated focus.
- The AI claim tools are listed under its enterprise and multidisciplinary offerings, so smaller ABA practices should confirm what their package includes.


## 10. AdvancedMD


**What it is:** Medical office software that the company says serves 13,000 private practices and 850 medical billing companies, with a mental health bundle of EHR, teletherapy, scheduling and billing.


**Best for:** Multi-specialty practices with mental health providers, mental health group practices, and billing companies that serve them.


**Strengths:**


- Cloud-hosted billing with an integrated clearinghouse, eligibility checks, and ClaimInspector scrubbing for CCI, HIPAA and LCD errors
- ERA processing that matches payments and builds prioritized worklists for denials and unexpected payment amounts
- Centralized billing across providers and locations, a managed RCM service, and group scheduling and group notes


**Watch-outs:**


- A general medical platform configured for mental health, so SUD programs with residential or institutional billing should confirm fit.
- The free trial targets practices of 1 to 3 providers; larger groups go through a demo and custom pricing.


## 11. Tebra


**What it is:** A platform for independent practices combining EHR, billing, payments and patient engagement, with a mental health offering for therapy and psychiatry practices.


**Best for:** Independent therapy and psychiatry practices, and practices that want better billing without changing EHRs.


**Strengths:**


- Time-based billing that maps session length to the correct CPT codes, and billing for one-on-one or group virtual sessions
- Claim submission that detects common errors and applies payer-specific rules, plus automated eligibility
- Automated ERA posting, an A/R dashboard that surfaces denial patterns, and paths for in-house billers (no EHR switch required) or vetted billing partners


**Watch-outs:**


- Built for independent practices across specialties, so multi-level SUD programs will find treatment center platforms closer to their workflows.
- Outsourced billing runs through partner firms, a second company to evaluate.


## The layer billing software does not cover


Most billing systems are built to answer one question well: is this claim complete, coded and formatted the way the payer expects? Many medical necessity denials and audit findings turn on a different question: does the chart behind the claim support it?


That question lives in the documentation. Did the assessment justify the ASAM level of care billed? Does the note show[medical necessity](https://blog.adentris.com/medical-necessity-documentation-behavioral-health/) for this service on this date? Was the treatment plan signed on time? Is a valid Part 2 consent in place? A claim can pass every scrubber and still fail on those points months later.


Billing software Pre-bill documentation review


**Works on** The claim The chart behind the claim


**Typical checks** Eligibility, codes, modifiers, authorization numbers, payer formatting Level of care justification, medical necessity, plan and signature timing, Part 2 consent


**When problems surface** Before submission (claim errors) and at remittance (denials) Before submission, while the note can still be corrected


Pre-bill[documentation compliance](https://adentris.com/solutions/documentation-compliance?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=internal&utm_campaign=best-behavioral-health-billing-software&utm_content=inline) sits between the EHR and the billing system. It reviews the chart against payer and regulatory rules before the claim goes out, so gaps get fixed while the clinician still remembers the session. Because it reads the chart, not the claim, it works with any billing system.


This is the layer Adentris covers. It works on top of any EHR, connecting through its API or FHIR, HL7 feeds, an API our agents build where none exists, or the AI Web Agent, usually with no IT project on your side, and is typically live in about 30 days. It reviews every active chart, not a sample, against payer and regulatory rules before claims go out, including ASAM level of care, medical necessity, 42 CFR Part 2, Medicaid and payer documentation rules, and treatment plan and signature timing. Each finding cites the rule that fired, with a drafted correction for staff to approve. At[Solutions 2 Recovery](https://adentris.com/case-studies/solutions-2-recovery?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=internal&utm_campaign=best-behavioral-health-billing-software&utm_content=inline) , a full-continuum SUD provider in Los Angeles that runs on Kipu, documentation conformance rose 22% in three weeks, and the largest cause of findings was two fields missing from a template.


## How to choose


1. **Start with your levels of care and claim types.** List every service line you bill and which go out on professional or institutional claims. Rule out any system that cannot handle all of them.
2. **Map your authorization load.** If most revenue depends on authorizations, utilization review tracking matters more than patient payment features.
3. **Decide who does the billing.** Software only, software plus a vendor billing team (Valant, Qualifacts, Netsmart, CentralReach, AdvancedMD), or partner firms (TherapyNotes, Tebra).
4. **Demo with your hardest cases.** A large group session, an authorization expiring mid-week, a residential to IOP step-down and a denial with a remark code.
5. **Check the reports you will live in.** Denials by reason code and payer, A/R aging by program, and authorization utilization.
6. **Plan the documentation layer.** Decide how charts get checked before claims go out: in the EHR, by a QA team, or with a pre-bill review tool.


As a starting point: solo or small outpatient practices, TherapyNotes, SimplePractice or Tebra; outpatient groups with IOP or PHP, Valant; SUD and residential centers, Kipu Health or Sunwave Health; agencies and CCBHCs, Qualifacts or Netsmart; ABA, CentralReach; multi-specialty practices and billing companies, AdvancedMD or Tebra.


## Common pitfalls to avoid


- **Choosing on the clinical demo alone.** Have your billing lead run part of every demo.
- **Buying for the program you have, not the one you are building.** If you plan to add IOP, PHP or residential care, confirm institutional claims and utilization review now.
- **Treating a clean claim as a defensible claim.** Scrubbers check the claim; medical necessity and level of care live in the chart.
- **Keeping authorizations in spreadsheets.** If authorization dates are not in the system that builds claims, expirations get discovered at denial.
- **Assuming outsourced billing transfers documentation risk.** A billing team can work denials faster, but it cannot add documentation that was never written.

## Frequently asked questions


**What is the best behavioral health billing software?**


It depends on your organization. Outpatient therapy and psychiatry practices usually fit practice suites such as TherapyNotes, SimplePractice, Valant or Tebra. SUD treatment centers often fit Kipu Health or Sunwave Health, agencies and CCBHCs Qualifacts or Netsmart, ABA providers CentralReach, and multi-specialty practices AdvancedMD. To automate billing, coding and denial work without replacing your systems, add Adentris on top.


**What is the best billing software for a small mental health practice?**


Practice suites with billing built into the EHR, such as TherapyNotes, SimplePractice and Tebra, are designed for solo and small group practices, and Valant and AdvancedMD serve them too. Compare claim scrubbing, ERA posting, and whether billing help is available.


**What billing software do substance abuse treatment centers use?**


Treatment centers with detox, residential, PHP and IOP programs typically need a platform that builds claims from attendance or census data and tracks utilization review, such as Kipu Health or Sunwave Health (which now includes Lightning Step). Larger SUD agencies also evaluate Qualifacts and Netsmart.


**Is billing software the same as RCM services?**


No. Billing software is the system your team uses to check eligibility, submit claims, post payments and work denials; RCM services are people who do that work for you. Valant, Qualifacts, Netsmart, CentralReach and AdvancedMD offer both, while TherapyNotes and Tebra connect practices with billing partners.


**Can billing software prevent denials?**


It prevents many technical denials by checking eligibility, codes, modifiers and payer formatting before submission. Denials driven by documentation, such as missing medical necessity or an unjustified level of care, have to be prevented in the chart, which is the job of pre-bill documentation review.


**Do I have to switch EHRs to improve billing?**


Not always. Tebra says in-house billers can use its billing tools without switching EHRs, and Netsmart says its revenue cycle solutions are EHR-agnostic. Pre-bill documentation review such as Adentris also works on top of the EHR you already have.
